output:
Four households are billed in groups that a signed householding agreement contradicts: **HH-0586, HH-0592, HH-0928 and HH-4821**.

I searched the CRM of all 92 households. Only these four have a signed agreement of kind "householding". All four follow the same pattern. A letter signed by all three family members says the joint account, a spouse's IRA and an adult child's individual account "are billed together as one group from the next billing cycle". As of 15 April 2026, the portfolio system still bills them in two groups: the joint account and IRA in one, the child's account alone in the other. Both groups were last changed on the date the child's advisory agreement was signed, in 2021, which is before each householding letter. So the split was never updated.

| Household | Householding agreement (signed) | Billing groups (last changed) |
|---|---|---|
| HH-0592 Haddad | AGR-0592-3 (2023-10-20) | BG-0592-1 (joint + Bilal's IRA) / BG-0592-2 (Fatima) – 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0928 Jablonski | AGR-0928-3 (2024-03-05) | BG-0928-1 (joint + Hugo's IRA) / BG-0928-2 (Nikhil) – 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0586 Quarshie | AGR-0586-3 (2024-06-07) | BG-0586-1 (joint + Saoirse's IRA) / BG-0586-2 (Amara) – 2021-09-01 |
| HH-4821 Okafor-Lind | AGR-4821-3 (2024-11-18) | BG-4821-1 (joint + Henrik's IRA) / BG-4821-2 (Ngozi) – 2021-09-14 |

I looked for anything that might explain the split and found nothing:
- **Accounts and parties:** The custodian's account records match the agreements. Every account is open and owned by the people who signed.
- **Later records:** No CRM note or activity revokes or replaces any of the letters. The 2025-10-14 annual review in each household says "No changes requested".
- **Billing files:** All four use the standard fee schedule with no exceptions noted.

Two things I ruled out:
- **HH-7350:** Billed in two groups, but its CRM says Aiko "has not agreed to household billing", so the split is correct.
- **Other "billed with" wording:** Several advisory agreements (not householding agreements) say an account is "billed with" or "billed together" with others. They fall outside the question, so I didn't check them against billing.

This matters for fees because the schedule is tiered (1.00% up to $1M, 0.80% to $2M, 0.60% above) and charged per billing group. Billing these accounts apart can put them in higher tiers than one combined group would. I haven't worked out the overcharge for any household.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households are billed in groups that a signed householding agreement contradicts?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households are, "none_found" if none is, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household that is, each as {"household_id": ..., "agreement_id": the householding agreement, "billing_group_ids": the billing groups that hold its accounts apart, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
